data.title: Mrityunjay Athreya: the unfashionable management guru who shuns jargon for purpose
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- In 1967, when Mrityunjay Athreya returned to India from Harvard Business School, where he had just completed his doctorate in business administration, India's corporate environment was inward-looking and constrained by strict government controls.

The 26-year-old Athreya's return to his homeland, shunning the many lucrative options available to him in the US, came partly from a love for his country but also because he had figured that Indian companies needed strategic thinking and access to management ideas that were transforming the best companies across the world.

Born in 1941 in Tirunelveli, Tamil Nadu, into a large Tamil Brahmin family, his early education was at a Tamil-medium school before the family moved to Chennai, where he went on to study statistics at Loyola College and then won a gold medal on the way to qualifying as a cost accountant. The choice of subjects was driven by the demands of supplementing the family income, and it worked: he immediately got a job with the British engineering company Guest Keen Williams in Calcutta as a cost accountant.

Ambitious and self-confident, Athreya soon applied to American universities for an MBA programme, though his application went with a twist: Athreya argued that, given his degree and professional qualifications, he should get direct admission to a PhD programme. Stanford Graduate School of Business was among those that agreed, and that's where he proceeded as a Hoover Fellow. A year later, he transferred to Harvard as a Ford Fellow.

On completion, influenced by his childhood hero Subhas Chandra Bose, he chose to come back home, recognising the need and the opportunity to transform Indian companies stuck in a strategy rut. To start with, he joined the Indian Institute of Management in Calcutta as an assistant professor, teaching strategic planning and behavioural sciences. Alongside, he also started consulting and was part of a committee in 1971 set up by the government to restructure the floundering Indian Airlines. After six years of teaching and consulting, he went on a three-year sabbatical to teach at the London Business School.

On his return, he set himself up as an independent adviser to companies, associations, governments and NGOs. It was a good time to become a management consultant in India. The likes of McKinsey, BCG, Arthur D. Little and Monitor had little interest in the country.

Starting off with an assignment for Bharat Heavy Electric Ltd, then part of a set of emerging public sector companies, he went on to advise Indian Oil Corporation, NTPC and ONGC, as well as private firms such as Mahindra & Mahindra and Bharat Forge.

It would take another decade for global consulting majors to make their way into the country, and even then they came in with Western models and ideas. By then, Athreya had tested and deployed his own thinking, which stressed that management was more about people, purpose, values and getting everyone to function as a cohesive team.

In the 1990s, amidst the exhilaration of liberalization that brought a rash of multinational consulting firms along with fashionable management jargon, Athreya sounded almost old-school. Yet, when it came to restructuring India's moribund telecom services infrastructure, the government turned to him.

The Athreya Committee's recommendations, including breaking up the monolithic Department of Telecom, opening up some sections of the network to the private sector and the creation of an independent regulator for the sector, laid the foundations for a telecom revolution, perhaps the most successful government-led intervention in the country.

Typical of the man, he again changed track around 2007, increasingly devoting much of his time to the non-profit sector since he believed that civil society was a crucial leg of the trimurti comprising the government and business that was needed to solve the problems of India.

He was also spending more time with Sampradaan, the platform for charitable initiatives by high net worth individuals set up in 1996. Since then, his work has been more about incorporating Indian philosophical ideas like dharma, the Gita and Vedanta into management.

No longer satisfied with offering corporate advice, Athreya, now 85, likes to talk and deal with issues like lessons for Indian industry from China, governance, social enterprises, technology, inequality and climate change.

It is significant that even as many of the management fads of the 1990s and early 2000s have been debunked or heavily caveated, Athreya's more down-to-earth thinking and wisdom has stood the test of time.

data.title: The week in charts: rate hikes, SIP flows, Airtel's tariffs
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- From the Reserve Bank of India raising its key interest rate for the first time since February 2023 to record SIP inflows despite a shaky stock market, a temporary easing in the standoff over flight operations between Mumbai's two airports and airlines, Bharti Airtel raising postpaid tariffs, and India's 85-medal haul at the Asian Games-here is the week's news in numbers.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) raised its key interest rate by 25 basis points, taking the repo rate to 5.5% from 5.25% earlier. This was the first hike by the central bank since February 2023. The RBI also adopted a hawkish stance, signalling that more rate increases could follow as it seeks to contain inflation risks.

The move comes as several major central banks have also turned more cautious on inflation, with higher energy prices and global trade uncertainty adding to price pressures. The rate increase is expected to raise borrowing costs for consumers, including for auto and housing loans, and weigh on credit growth. Economists expect further tightening in India: Yes Bank sees hikes of 1 percentage point in this cycle, while HDFC Bank expects increases of up to 0.75 percentage point.

Monthly inflows into mutual funds through systematic investment plans (SIPs) rose to an all-time high of Rs.32,297 crore in August, showing continued appetite among retail investors despite a shaky stock market. SIPs are periodic investment commitments by retail investors, typically monthly, and tend to be sticky in nature.

However, the record inflows came alongside a sharp rise in the number of SIPs being discontinued or reaching the end of their tenure. Data from industry grouping Amfi showed that 5.38 million SIPs were either discontinued or reached the end of their tenure in August-the most since January 2026. On a relative scale, the ratio of SIPs stopped to SIPs started was around 81% in August, suggesting that more investors were keen to enter the market than those who sought to exit.

The central government has asked Adani Airport Holdings to put on hold its plan to shift a portion of international flights from Mumbai airport to Navi Mumbai airport, temporarily easing a standoff with airlines. Adani operates both airports serving the Mumbai region. The Navi Mumbai airport began commercial operations in December 2025, after which Adani lined up the renovation of Terminal 1 at Mumbai airport.

As part of the plan, it asked airlines to shift one-third of their international flights from Mumbai's Terminal 2 to Navi Mumbai. Airlines, however, said they were not consulted on the proposed move. The Navi Mumbai airport recorded 3,047 aircraft movements in August, compared with 26,017 at Mumbai airport, and has seen aircraft movements decline over the past three months.

26%: The projected year-on-year increase in market borrowings by Indian states in the October-December quarter, to Rs.3.6 trillion, according to Icra.

Rs.28,000: The average price per sq ft of DLF's first senior-living project, The Aureva in Gurugram. All 172 apartments, with a total value of Rs.1,985 crore, were sold within days of the launch.

21%: The share of Indian stock brokers in commercial paper issuance in 2026, up from 4% in 2021. Brokers have raised about $33 billion, mainly to fund leveraged equity bets.

$102 million: The amount spent by Google co-founder Sergey Brin to oppose California's proposed billionaire wealth tax, making him the largest contributor to the campaign against it.

7: The number of countries, including India, that have expressed interest in hosting the 2036 Summer Olympics. The other six are Germany, Hungary, Qatar, South Africa, South Korea and Turkey.

India's second-largest telecom service provider Bharti Airtel has increased the prices of its postpaid plans by about 3-11%, its largest such price hike since 2024. The move comes days ahead of the expected initial public offering (IPO) of Jio Platforms, the parent of Reliance Jio, which is India's largest telecom operator by subscribers.

A raise in tariffs by Airtel could pave the way for Jio to follow suit, potentially giving it an opportunity to increase prices. Airtel last raised its headline tariffs in June 2024, after a gap of two years, following Jio. In the first quarter of 2026-27, Airtel recorded an average revenue per user (ARPU) of Rs.264. The company has been raising its ARPU, but the pace of annual growth has varied, with 2025-26 recording the lowest increase over a five-year period.

India finished the 2026 Asian Games with 85 medals, as a late gold rush helped it retain fourth place in the medals table behind China, Japan and South Korea. Its tally, however, was 21 medals lower than the 106 it won at the 2022 Hangzhou Asiad. India won medals in 20 of the 43 sports at this year's Games, but 76 of its 85 medals came from just 11 sports.

Athletics and shooting remained its two biggest medal-winning sports, although India won fewer medals in both than it did in 2022. The performance was unchanged from 2022 in seven of the other 11 sports that contributed to this year's tally, while India won more medals in the remaining two-boxing and golf.

data.title: Is HAL stock priced for perfection? What to expect over the next 5 years
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- Indian defence stocks have faced periods of selling pressure over the past year after a strong multi-year rally.

Concerns around elevated valuations, profit booking, execution delays, and supply-chain challenges have led to sharp corrections across several defence names, including Hindustan Aeronautics (HAL).

HAL has posted negative returns of 1.47% over the past year, according to NSE data, compared to a positive 1.62% return for the Nifty Next 50 index.

Today, we examine the factors that could determine where HAL's stock could be in the next five years. But first, let's find out what the company is all about.

HAL is a major Indian aerospace and defence company that manufactures and maintains fighter aircraft, helicopters, aircraft engines, and other aerospace systems.

It is also involved in the development and production of platforms such as the Tejas light combat aircraft and Dhruv helicopters, as well as providing repair, overhaul, and maintenance services.

HAL entered FY27 with a robust order book of Rs.2.54 trillion. Management expects further growth in its deal pipeline, with key contracts-including 143 Advanced Light Helicopters (ALH) for the Indian Army, the IAF's Su-30 fleet upgrade, and the modernization of 40 Dornier Do-228 aircraft-currently at various stages of clearance.

In total, the company expects to bag fresh orders worth Rs.90,000 crore over the next two years, including repair and overhaul (ROH) contracts. However, its long-term performance hinges heavily on its ability to execute and deliver on these commitments on time.

To meet its large existing order book, handle anticipated new contracts, and ensure timely client deliveries, HAL has expanded manufacturing capacity for major programs. Production of the Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) and HTT-40 basic trainer has been scaled up across its Bengaluru and Nashik facilities, while Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) manufacturing at the Bengaluru and Tumakuru plants remains a core focus going forward.

Looking ahead, HAL plans to build dedicated manufacturing infrastructure for the LCA Mark-II, GE 414 engines, and Indian Multi-Role Helicopter (IMRH) engines. The expansion plan also includes infrastructure for Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV) manufacturing, aero-engine indigenization projects, and design and development facilities for the IMRH and other defense programs.

The firm plans to invest about Rs.12,000 crore in these capital expenditure projects by 2030. Successfully converting this order book into timely deliveries and revenue recognition will be a decisive driver of the stock's performance over the next five years.

On top-line performance, HAL management remains confident of sustaining double-digit revenue growth through FY26 and FY27. On profitability, the company aims to protect its historically strong Ebitda margin baseline of 30-31%.

HAL remains a net debt-free company. Over the past five years, it has delivered consistent bottom-line performance, posting an average net profit growth of 22.9%. Also, its robust internal cash generation provides sufficient liquidity to fund upcoming capital expenditure plans.

HAL builds complex defense platforms such as the Tejas LCA and Light Combat Helicopters, requiring thousands of intricate components spanning avionics, engines, and weapon systems. In advanced aerospace manufacturing where tolerance for error is minimal, a single glitch during design, testing, or assembly can trigger multi-month operational delays. Having previously faced setbacks such as delayed General Electric (GE) engine deliveries, execution bottlenecks remain one of the primary risks facing the company.

Foreign-sourced critical parts expose HAL to delays, import restrictions, and cost volatility, amplifying execution bottlenecks despite. Manpower shortages for skilled engineers and MSME supply chain gaps further hinder scaling production to meet strict ministry of defence timelines.

According to a recent ICRA report, sales to the Indian defence forces account for more than 90% of the company's operating revenue. Although the company is trying to diversify its revenue base by increasing the share of orders from other clients and exports, a single customer still contributes heavily.

HAL trades at a price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of 34.5, which is above its five-year median P/E of 30.7. Also, at a price-to-book (P/B) multiple of 7.3, the stock's valuation appears rich.

HAL's long-term growth prospects remain bright, anchored by a massive order backlog, expanding national defense budgets, solid balance sheet fundamentals, and the government's push for local manufacturing.

However, the stock's performance over the next five years will hinge entirely on execution, specifically HAL's capacity to convert its order pipeline into timely deliveries and recognized revenue. Seamless production scaling across the Tejas fighter and helicopter programs, engine availability, and supply chain management will be paramount.

At 34.5 times earnings, the stock offers limited valuation cushion, meaning any project execution delays could weigh on shareholder returns.

Investors should always evaluate a company's fundamentals, corporate governance, and stock valuations before making an investment decision.

Happy investing!

data.title: Best of the Week | An 'epiphany', a complaint and 36 caveats: Inside the Tata Trusts rift
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- Best of the Week is a weekly newsletter by Siddharth Sharma/Shravani Sinha. Subscribe to Mint's newsletters to get them directly in your inbox.

The Tata boardroom drama has now moved into the trustees' room, and the letters are getting sharper.

Noel Tata and three fellow trustees of the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) have sent a five-page letter to colleagues Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh. Its target is their public backing for listing Tata Sons, which the letter sarcastically calls an "epiphany" that struck in April. The four say the pair never raised the idea at three SDTT board meetings since April and chose the media over their co-trustees instead. The letter also lays bare the arithmetic inside SDTT: four trustees on one side, two on the other.

SDTT owns 27.98% of Tata Sons, the holding company of India's largest conglomerate, and the letter says the Trusts' settled position has long been to keep it unlisted. Then came 17 September, when the Tata Sons board outvoted Noel to give N Chandrasekaran a third term as chairman and began moving towards a listing. Srinivasan voted with the majority.

There is a procedural sub-plot too. After the board backed a listing, Tata Trusts suggested on 28 September that Tata Sons could merge two subsidiaries to drop their core investment company and non-banking financial company tags. Singh and Srinivasan said they were not consulted. The four trustees counter that the Tata Sons board itself asked the Trusts to work on options for complying with the RBI's communication, and that Srinivasan was in the room.

Now the regulator has entered the picture. On 25 September, Srinivasan and Singh filed complaints with the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner, alleging SDTT's direct involvement in Tata Sons' commercial affairs and interference with the independent decision-making of nominee directors. Srinivasan has also urged action against any wrongdoing an investigation finds, including the possible suspension or removal of Noel as SDTT chairman. The commissioner has given SDTT until 12 October to reply.

Noel's camp sees an irony. The two who are asking for collective deliberation, they say, had already asked the regulator to stop the trustees from meeting at all, and never told the Trusts about their complaints. The four trustees now hope both complaints will be withdrawn. Will they be?

Precedent adds spice. In May, the commissioner barred the Sir Ratan Tata Trust, which owns 23.56% of Tata Sons, from holding meetings or taking decisions, after Srinivasan alleged that its permanent trustees exceeded a state limit.

Noel and his son Neville are not waiting around. On 1 October, they filed 21 and 15 caveats respectively with the commissioner, hoping to be heard before any order lands. The timing is interesting, because the Trusts' combined 65.9% voting power in Tata Sons could count for a great deal.

Meanwhile, the letter insists the Trusts neither run Tata Sons nor seek to. Their shareholding is the principal asset funding their charitable work, it says, and protecting it is stewardship, not business. Srinivasan and Singh see things very differently, and that disagreement may now be for the regulator to weigh.

The RBI's first rate hike in nearly four years was only the opening act. Now the aftershocks are arriving. Borrowers are bracing for higher EMIs or longer tenures, and consumer stocks have already slipped as investors fear a hit to festive spending. Banks, flush with liquidity, may find the hike a welcome cushion for their margins. Behind it all is inflation. Economists polled by Mint expect September's retail inflation to hit a 23-month high, with pressure spreading beyond a few food items. The central bank has also signalled that more hikes may follow.

Washington's visa crackdown is hitting trouble in court, yet opening a new front elsewhere. Two US courts have pushed Trump's $100,000 H-1B fee towards a dead end, finding the administration overreached. But the White House has not blinked. The US has now suspended green card labour certifications for six big outsourcing firms, including TCS, Infosys and Wipro, citing ongoing investigations. For India's IT majors, the immediate damage may be limited. They account for under 2% of such applications, and existing employees can keep working. The bigger worry is: what happens to the talent these firms most want to keep?

Mumbai airport's makeover has turned into a tug of war, and passengers are caught in the middle. Adani-run MIAL wanted to cut about a third of weekly international departure slots from 25 October to make room during Terminal 1's rebuild, with some flights heading to Navi Mumbai, 50 km away. Airlines said no, pointing to schedules approved months ago and asking why the cuts were needed. Now the civil aviation ministry has hit pause and sent everyone back to find common ground after 13 October. Adani insists the move is temporary. But for flyers, a different airport could mean higher fees and messier connections.

Angel One once won customers with printed research and branch networks. Then the internet rewrote the rules, and it went fully digital. Now the 30-year-old broker is reinventing itself again. It has shed nearly a fifth of its workforce as rivals Groww and Zerodha pull ahead on profits. Tighter derivatives rules and a shrinking pool of active investors are squeezing the business that once fuelled its growth. Its answer is a "super app" that bundles broking, mutual funds, insurance and credit under one roof. The bet is that existing customers will do more with the company.

India has become cheaper, yet foreign investors keep heading for the exit. That is the mystery haunting Dalal Street. Through September, net foreign equity outflows hit Rs.2.60 trillion, and the Nifty trailed every global peer Mint tracked. Meanwhile, Asian rivals riding the AI and semiconductor wave raced ahead.

But look at the primary market and the story shifts. Foreign investors have been net buyers there every single month this year. So have they really given up on India, or are they simply getting choosier? And what would it take to bring them back? Experts point to earnings upgrades, a steadier rupee and softer crude.

After building a Rs.48,178 crore-income lending business, Shriram Group is making a bigger push into capital markets, betting on India's growing appetite for investments. Its revamped business will combine broking, mutual funds and wealth management, using digital tools alongside human advice to reach investors beyond big cities.

The group is rebuilding Way2Wealth as an advice-led platform, with plans to expand margin trading finance. But the timing is tricky: volatile, range-bound markets threaten brokerage revenues, while established players dominate the space. Can Shriram turn its vast lending customer base into a new generation of investors?

Sebi's investor protection fund has nearly quadrupled to Rs.969.8 crore in FY26, but spending has barely budged. The regulator used just Rs.4.7 crore, or 0.4% of the corpus, even as financial-influencer scams, online investment frauds and digital arrests proliferate. A Sebi survey found 62% of investors base some or most investment decisions on finfluencer recommendations. The underutilization has caught the government's attention, though no decision has been made on intervention. Experts argue the fund could do more, from financing cybersecurity research to expanding investor awareness, while calling for greater transparency on spending and outcomes.

India's staffing firms are moving beyond supplying workers to being accountable for their performance. Quess Corp, TeamLease Services and Adecco are seeing growing demand for output-based billing, where vendors face penalties or lose fees if workers miss client targets.

About 10-15% of Quess clients already seek some form of output-driven service. The model can command fees of 10-20% per candidate, compared with 9-10% under traditional staffing. Rising labour costs and absenteeism are driving adoption, while AI-led productivity gains are pushing clients to pay for outcomes rather than activity. Adoption remains at an early stage.

Mercedes-Benz and BMW are bringing global models to India faster, shrinking launch delays from 10-12 months to around 4-6 months as buyers demand access to the latest vehicles. Mercedes plans to introduce its GLC electric model six months after its European debut, while BMW has brought some performance models within three to four months.

Right-hand-drive conversions and regulatory certification remain hurdles. The push reflects India's growing importance and rising demand for premium vehicles. Mercedes sold a record 15,190 cars in January-September 2026, up 8% year-on-year, while BMW's April-June deliveries rose 17% to 4,507.

Women's commutes in India reveal a stark gender divide, according to the first National Household Travel Survey, covering 1.8 million people. The share of rural women travelling over 1 km to work is just 37.7%, against 64.2% travelling for education. In cities, the share falls from 67.5% to 52.9%. Rural women largely walk to work, while urban women rely more on buses and other public transport. Men depend heavily on two-wheelers. Safety also shapes travel patterns, with women generally leaving work earlier. Men typically spend more on commuting each month.

That's all from us this week. Subscribe to our newsletters and the website for what's in the news and beyond it. Write to us at newsletters@livemint.com.

data.title: SpaceX's Spectrum Deal Could Boost AST SpaceMobile’s Strategic Value — Analyst Calls ASTS 'Natural Satellite Partner' For Carriers
data.description:
Key points:
  • Berenberg maintained a ‘Buy’ rating on AST SpaceMobile following Grain Management’s agreement to sell its nationwide spectrum portfolio to SpaceX.
  • According to Filatov, SpaceX's decision to build out its own network could make AST SpaceMobile “more strategically relevant” rather than simply increasing competitive pressure.
  • He cited SpaceX positioning itself as a mobile carrier rather than simply a satellite connectivity provider as the reason for his optimism around AST SpaceMobile.

Space Exploration Technologies Corp.’s (SPCX) latest push into mobile connectivity could be creating an unexpected opportunity for AST SpaceMobile Inc. (ASTS), analysts at Berenberg said.

The satellite-to-phone race is increasingly becoming a battle over not just technology, but who ultimately controls the customer relationship. According to TheFly, Berenberg analyst Michael Filatov believes SpaceX’s latest move could sharpen the strategic distinction between the two companies.

AST SpaceMobile shares fell more than 10% on Friday, declining 0.1% further during the after-hours trade. SpaceX shares gained more than 1% during the regular trading session, and rose 0.1% further in the after-hours trade.

SpaceX’s Mobile Ambitions Could Boost ASTS

Berenberg maintained a ‘Buy’ rating on AST SpaceMobile following Grain Management’s agreement to sell its nationwide spectrum portfolio to SpaceX, subject to Federal Communications Commission approval.

The deal involves up to 14 MHz of paired spectrum in the 800 MHz band, giving SpaceX access to low-band spectrum that it says will help close a key technical gap for its Starlink Mobile ambitions.

SpaceX described the move as a step toward building the world’s “most advanced” mobile network. The company said the low-band spectrum will complement its existing 2 GHz mid-band spectrum, with the new frequencies providing a coverage layer capable of improving connectivity through obstacles such as walls.

Critically, SpaceX said most existing mobile devices already support the band, potentially allowing Starlink Mobile to provide connectivity without requiring users to replace their phones.

SpaceX said its goal is to combine its satellite constellation with a terrestrial network into a single architecture that can provide connectivity “indoors, outdoors, in cellular dead zones, and everywhere in between.”

Berenberg sees that strategy as an important development for AST SpaceMobile.

ASTS Could Become The ‘Natural Satellite Partner’

According to Filatov, SpaceX's decision to build out its own network could make AST SpaceMobile “more strategically relevant” rather than simply increasing competitive pressure. He cited SpaceX positioning itself as a mobile carrier rather than simply a satellite connectivity provider as the reason for his optimism around AST SpaceMobile.

That could leave ASTS with a potentially valuable position in the market, which is partnering with existing telecom operators rather than competing against them, the analyst said.

Filatov argues that AST SpaceMobile is currently the only device-to-device operator whose technology is designed to deliver broadband connectivity to existing smartphones while maintaining a carrier-partnership model.

The analyst therefore sees AST SpaceMobile as “the natural satellite partner for operators.”

SPCX Gets Another Boost From FCC

The spectrum deal wasn't SpaceX’s only major mobile-network milestone this week.

The FCC also approved SpaceX’s Gen2 Starlink constellation application, authorizing the company to launch 15,000 satellites optimized for 2 GHz spectrum globally.

SpaceX said its V2 Starlink Mobile satellites will deliver more than 100 times the bandwidth of its current generation and provide high-speed connectivity directly to unmodified devices.

The FCC also authorized the full range of backhaul bands used by SpaceX’s V3 broadband satellites, allowing them to operate with Starlink’s existing gateway network.

SpaceX said the approvals will help advance its vision of keeping users connected “no matter where they are,” from dense cities to remote and rural areas.

What Retail Investors Think About ASTS Stock

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around AST SpaceMobile trended in the ‘bullish’ territory at the time of writing.

ASTS stock is down 30% year-to-date, while SPCX stock is up 8%. The Vanguard Morningstar Total Stock Market ETF (VTI) is up 16% over the past 12 months, while the Vanguard Morningstar Small-Cap ETF (VB) is up 13%.

data.title: RBI steps up rupee support, opens dollar window for oil companies
data.description:
Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has announced more ​measures to support the rupee on Saturday after the ‌currency fell to within striking distance of ​its record low.

RBI will open a special window to meet the daily dollar requirements of three government oil-marketing companies to ‌ease the pressure on the spot market.

Under such an arrangement, used in ‌times of strain on the currency, the RBI ‌provides ⁠oil companies dollars directly from its foreign ⁠exchange reserves.

Indian Oil, Hindustan Petroleum and Bharat Petroleum will be allowed to access dollars under the facility from ​Monday, the RBI said.

Forex dealers will not permit users to rebook any foreign exchange derivatives, the bank said.

The RBI slashed the limit for positions in ‌exchange-traded currency derivatives involving the rupee to $5 million ​from $100 million.

The central bank asked forex dealers to maintain a “foreign exchange risk reserve” ⁠for all derivative contracts involving the rupee equal to 20 per cent of the notional amount of each transaction.

The RBI has raised dollars and hiked its policy rate, but pressure on the currency has persisted. On Friday, the rupee closed at 96.73 per dollar, barely changed from its previous close, and near its all-time weakest level of 96.96, hit in ‌May.

The rupee rallied in the non-deliverable forward market ​on Saturday, with the one-month dollar/rupee contract falling about 40 paise in very thin trading, ⁠one trader said.

Addressing oil companies’ dollar requirements ⁠removes one of the largest sources of demand from the FX market, which should help reduce ‌volatility but it will show up in a depletion of reserves, said Dhiraj Nim, FX ​strategist at ANZ Bank in Mumbai.

data.title: Wall Street posts weekly gains with earnings, inflation data on tap
data.description:
Wall Street ended higher on Friday as investors shifted their focus to ​next week, with third-quarter earnings season set to start and inflation data expected, which could shed light on the Federal Reserve's ‌next policy decision.

All three major US stock indexes advanced on the day, logging weekly gains. The small-cap Russell 2000, however, ended lower than last Friday's close.

"It's the kind of back-and-forth market we've been in where we have the reversal of sentiment around Iran," said Ross Mayfield, investment strategy analyst at Baird in Louisville, Kentucky. "With conflicting headlines coming out of ​the White House and parties in the Middle East, there's just no edge there."

"That's why it's a fairly tepid rally," Mayfield added.

Crude ​prices initially retreated after President Donald Trump said the US will not launch any attacks on Iran before the midterm ⁠elections, adding that talks between Washington and Tehran aimed at ending the market-rattling Iran war were "productive."

Front-month West Texas Intermediate oil and Brent crude both settled ​up 0.4%.

Benchmark Treasury yields edged higher, but remained below Wednesday's 24-year high.

BANKS DUE TO REPORT EARNINGS

Third-quarter reporting season begins in earnest next week, with big ​US banks Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and Morgan Stanley scheduled to release results.

Analysts estimate S&P 500 annual earnings growth of 30.6%, on aggregate, for the July-September period, with energy and technology posting the largest year-on-year earnings growth of 123% and 66.5%, respectively, according to LSEG data.

The mood of American consumers, who shoulder about ​70% of the US economy, has soured this month, according to the University of Michigan, with near-term expectations deteriorating to an all-time low.

The Dow Jones ​Industrial Average rose 423.31 points, or 0.83%, to 51,654.95, the S&P 500 gained 46.15 points, or 0.59%, to 7,811.51 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 172.83 points, or 0.64%, ‌to 27,366.17.

Among ⁠the 11 major sectors of the S&P 500, communication services (.SPLRCL), opens new tab was the lone percentage loser.

AI-related momentum stocks were generally higher, with the Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF up 1% as the US bull market, largely driven by the AI boom, approaches its four-year anniversary.

"Chips have been this year's story," said Michael Monaghan, portfolio manager at Founder ETFs in Dallas. "(It's) a multidecade technological change and just at the beginning of whatever's happening, not at the end."

Elon Musk's SpaceX struck a deal to ​acquire a nationwide low-band spectrum portfolio, ​posing a direct challenge to US ⁠wireless companies. Telecom firms T-Mobile US, AT&T, and Verizon dropped between 8.8% and 13.3%.

Humana jumped 11.6% after US government data showed 95% of the health insurer's members were in Medicare Advantage plans rated four stars or higher for ​2027.

data.title: BlackRock ETF clients buy $22.38 million worth of Bitcoin
data.description:
BlackRock's Bitcoin ETF clients added $22.38 million worth of Bitcoin, extending the fund's pattern of steady, if uneven, demand.

Farside Investors data shows the iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) recorded a net inflow of $22.4 million on October 9, 2026.

A net inflow is simple arithmetic. It is the money investors put into the fund minus the money they pulled out.

BlackRock does not keep that Bitcoin in its own vault. Custody of IBIT's holdings sits with Coinbase Prime, the institutional arm of the US exchange.

The October 9 inflow came during a choppy stretch for the fund. On October 7, IBIT saw a $207.7 million outflow, a far larger move in the opposite direction.

Earlier in October, the fund pulled in $195.6 million within the first week of the month.

Bitcoin's price has recently hovered in a range between $78,700 and $85,000.

IBIT is BlackRock's flagship US spot Bitcoin ETF. A spot ETF holds the actual asset rather than futures contracts, so every share is backed by real Bitcoin.

The fund is the largest US spot Bitcoin ETF by assets under management, and leads the category in cumulative flows. Total inflows since launch have exceeded $65 billion.

Broader US spot Bitcoin ETF flows were mixed in early October 2026. IBIT often led inflows on positive days, while the category as a whole saw periods of net outflows.

In July 2026, BlackRock cut the minimum threshold for in-kind Bitcoin-to-IBIT conversions from $25 million to $1 million. data.title: Life insurers projected to post 10-20% VNB growth in 2QFY27: Report
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- Life insurance companies in India are likely to register a 10 to 20 per cent year-on-year growth in value of new business (VNB) during the second quarter of FY27, even as broader discussions focus heavily on proposed regulatory guidelines rather than quarterly operational prints, according to a research report by Kotak Institutional Equities.

The brokerage noted that private life insurers under its coverage show steady underwriting performance, driven largely by solid expansion in protection plans despite moderate annualised premium equivalent (APE) growth.

"We expect 2QFY27 earnings call discussion and stock price performance to be centered around the impact of the proposed distribution norms and EoM guidelines, with less emphasis on the quarterly financial performance itself," the report stated.

"Growth in protection is supporting margins and VNB despite moderate (10-15% yoy for the private sector) APE growth. Health claims tend to inch up in 2Q, though secular improvements and higher leverage continue to drive core earnings; trends in motor TP claims provisioning will drive the performance of non-life companies for the quarter. PB will continue on a steady growth path," the report added.

Analyzing company-level performances across the life insurance basket, the brokerage projects private insurers to record 10 to 15 per cent APE growth with a 6 to 18 per cent increase in VNB, alongside net margin shifts ranging between negative 200 basis points and positive 150 basis points. State-owned Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) is projected to outpace private peers on profitability, delivering an estimated 320 basis points of margin expansion to 22.5 per cent on the back of higher non-participating product share, which drives a 40 per cent surge in its VNB.

"We expect private life insurers under coverage to deliver 10-15% APE growth with 6-18% growth in VNB. We bake in -200 to +150 bps expansion in margins. The positive drivers are high growth in the protection business, ending the controversy on margin loss due to GST exemption. We do not expect a notable product mix change in the savings business," the report said.

Regarding the wider regulatory and medium-term operational environment, the research agency highlighted that proposed caps on expenses of management (EoM) and distribution commissions represent the primary variables shaping forward outlooks.

"With sweeping changes proposed in distribution payouts and EoM cap, we expect management discussions to be dominated by the same-loss of VNB due to likely lower credit protect business, channel strategy, open or closed architecture in banks, dependence on PB and ability to meet EoM norms," the report said.

It mentioned that the near-term growth outlook is likely to be strong due to the sunset period and the weakness in FY2028E (to initially adjust to new norms and then a high base) do not reflect the new normal.

"In the meanwhile, the IRDA will draft new norms on products, customer redressal and claims; we expect IFRS 17 and RBC to also be implemented. Hence, stocks will remain under pressure of uncertainty even as valuation remains un-demanding," the report stated.

In the non-life insurance space, claims ratios in motor third-party (TP) policies will set operating trends for the quarter following judicial pronouncements regarding homemaker compensation.

data.title: Green Card Woes Deepen for Indian Tech Workers
data.description:
Prachi Verma New Delhi: Thousands of Indian technology professionals pursuing US permanent residency face fresh uncertainty after the US suspended major technology companies, including Cognizant, Infosys, TCS, Wipro, HCLTech, Capgemini, Microsoft and Adobe, from the permanent labour certification (PERM) programme, an important step in the employer-sponsored green card process.

The move could delay permanent residency plans for employees already facing years-long green card backlogs, immigration experts told ET. Those nearing the six-year H-1B visa limit without an alternative basis for extension could face more immediate challenges, they added. "The immediate impact is on employment-based permanent-residence sponsorship, not on the subsistence of existing H-1B status," said Rohit Jain, managing partner at Singhania & Co. Existing H-1B approvals, approved I-140 petitions and permanent-resident status are not automatically revoked by this measure, he noted.

Employees awaiting PERM, however, may "face indefinite green-card delays, retention uncertainty and possible six-year H-1B-limit complications," Jain said. Close to a million Indians, including dependents, are estimated to be waiting for employment-based green cards, most of them in the EB-2 and EB-3 categories, said Sukanya Raman, country head for India at immigration-focused law firm Davies & Associates. "These are people who have spent years on temporary status and followed every rule, and now their green card process is on hold because of a dispute they have no part in," she added.

The restrictions could also become a talent-retention challenge for IT companies. While the firms are free to employ existing H-1B workers, their ability to offer those employees a long-term immigration pathway is constrained, said Sahil Nyati, founder and CEO of Meritmap and Jinee Green Card. "Employees may increasingly evaluate employers based not just on compensation and career growth, but also on the stability of their immigration sponsorship," he said.

Companies are reviewing their existing immigration pipelines. "They are identifying employees most exposed to the restrictions and reassessing their workforce planning," Nyati said. PERM requires an employer to establish that no able, willing, qualified and available US workers exist, and that employment of the foreign worker will not adversely affect equivalent US wages or conditions.

According to experts, IT employers are likely to apply a three-pronged strategy to address this - hire more US citizens and permanent residents, expand offshore and nearshore delivery capabilities, and become more selective about international employees. "We may also see companies evaluate alternative immigration pathways, including O-1A visas for individuals with extraordinary ability and EB-1A or EB-2 NIW green card categories for employees who independently qualify," Nyati said.

data.title: RBI Raises Minimum Daily CRR Maintenance to 99%
data.description:
to drain surplus liquidity Our Bureau Mumbai|Kolkata: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has raised the minimum daily cash reserve ratio (CRR) maintenance requirement for scheduled banks to 99% from 90%, effective from mid-October. The move is aimed at draining surplus liquidity in the banking system as the central bank shifts towards calibrated tightening amid a liquidity surplus of about 4 lakh crore.

In a notification on Friday, the RBI said banks will have to maintain a minimum daily balance of 99% of the CRR requirement from the fortnight beginning October 16. CRR is the amount of deposits banks maintain with the RBI without earning interest. The ratio currently stands at 3%, which means that out of every 100 of deposits, a bank has to keep 3 with the RBI without earning interest.

So far, banks have had the operational flexibility to maintain only 90% of the required amount without attracting penal action. "On a review of the current liquidity conditions, it has been decided to increase the minimum daily maintenance of the CRR from 90% of the requirement to 99% effective from the fortnight beginning October 16, 2026," the RBI said.

Bankers said the new measure will curtail operational freedom. "So far, in a fortnight, banks had the flexibility to maintain 90% of the required CRR amount for seven days and maintain 110% for the next half of the reporting fortnight so that the average comes out to 100%. That flexibility will now go as banks will mostly have to maintain 100% at all times.

Other than some operational changes, this new norm will not lead to any major changes for banks," said Gopal Tripathi, head-treasury and capital markets at Jana Small Finance Bank. The central bank has decided to raise the daily requirement instead of tinkering with the CRR rate, which, according to RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra's post-policy comments, is "the least preferred" tool. "RBI had offered CRR exemptions on FCNR (B) deposit inflows through the dedicated foreign currency mobilisation programme, and therefore any hike in the CRR would not drain the additional flows," said a treasury executive, who did not wish to be identified. In July 2013, the RBI had similarly increased the minimum daily CRR maintenance requirement to 99% from 70%, said people familiar with the matter.

data.title: GSFC Seeks Partner for Green Ammonia Factory in Gujarat

data.title: US Green Card Curbs may have Little Impact on Indian IT Cos
data.description:
Suspension from Permanent Labour Certification Tanya Pandey & Surabhi Agarwal New Delhi: The four Indian IT services companies suspended by the United States Labour Department from the employment-based green card process-Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Infosys, Wipro and HCLTech-together recorded just 61 certified Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) filings in the first nine months of fiscal 2026 (Oct 1, 2025-June 30, 2026), with HCL America recording 59 certified cases and TCS only two.

An ET analysis of US Department of Labour data shows that while American technology companies are bigger users of the programme, which allows foreign workers on H-1B visas to apply for permanent residency or the green card, employers in non-tech sectors such as food, meat and seafood were among the programme's biggest users.

TCS CEO K Krithivasan told ET on Friday that the suspension would have no impact on the company's business model or delivery of client projects, noting that its applications to convert H-1B visa holders to green-card holders had been in the single digits annually over the past two years. "We have close to 40,000 people in the US, and more than 50% of them are permanent residents or citizens," he said, adding that TCS files such applications occasionally when clients want the company to retain an employee for the long term. Foreign workers can stay in the US on an H-1B visa for six years, after which they have to return or apply for a green card. Consider the data for fiscal 2025. Of the 15 largest filers that year, five were technology companies and 10 were non-tech employers.

data.title: Food Industry Warns of Supply Shock as Super El NiÃ±o Threatens Crops
data.description:
Jayashree Bhosale Pune: India's food industry is warning of a potential supply shock in 2027 as a developing Super El NiÃ±o threatens to disrupt crop production, squeeze supplies and fuel food inflation beyond this year's monsoon season. "We are not so much worried for the next few months.

What concerns us is the next year-2027," said Bimal Kothari, president of the Indian Pulses and Grains Association, as the rabi chana harvest emerges a key determinant of the price of pulses. Sugar producers fear two difficult seasons ahead. "We are afraid that 2026-27 and 2027-28 can be extremely challenging for sugar production and availability," said Dilip Patil of the Indian Federation of Grain Energy.

Scientists have also warned of rising temperatures, heat stress and higher water demand. Commodity and weather experts have warned that India needs to plan for the long-term impact of El NiÃ±o. "The structural inflation risk in sugar is a 2027 problem, not a Diwali 2026 problem and the window to prepare for it is the next six months," sugar experts Dilip Patil and Shekhar Gaikwad wrote in their note on the sector-A Comfortable Diwali, an Uncomfortable 2027-presented to the Reserve Bank of India recently. "The 2026-27 balance sheet carries very little buffer, and the real inflation test will arrive in mid-2027, not in October 2026." The duo predicted that the ex-mill sugar prices could cross 50 per kilogram during June-October 2027 as the thin closing stock becomes the market's focal point.

On October 5, the El NiÃ±o-induced sea surface temperatures in the Pacific Ocean set a new record, and are predicted to increase further. Former earth sciences secretary Madhavan Rajeevan said the country needs to prepare well in advance. "We should expect continued influences of this strong El NiÃ±o during the coming months," he said on X. "The ensuing winter could be warmer than normal, followed by a potentially hot and challenging pre-monsoon season, with an increased risk of severe heat-wave events." As prices of tur, chana, urad and yellow peas have already risen, the industry is more worried about the next year. "The real challenge is 2027. We need to see how the rabi plantation takes place.

We have drought in Maharashtra and Karnataka, both the states are important for chana," said Kothari. There are concerns about production of oilseeds, in which India is already import dependent.

Expect a big impact on sugar and oilseeds output from the Super El NiÃ±o, said Atul Chaturvedi, director, Shree Renuka Sugars and head of the Asian Palm Oil Alliance. "Among oilseeds, soyabean and groundnut seem to be in serious trouble, while sugarcane in Karnataka and parts of Maharashtra is drying up due to water scarcity," he said. "Domestic edible oil and sugar production is bound to suffer significantly during kharif. It would be interesting to see how this drought is going to impact rabi and beyond." data.title: MD bats for data centre space , says demand and healthy returns could make it a strong long-term biz
data.description:
'CORRECTION OF PRICING architecture AN INDUSTRY PROBLEM' People have to pay for consumption... Entry-level, inclusive plans have to stay where they are Shashwat Sharma MD & CEO, Bharti Airtel Airtel ARPU Will Cross 300 Very Soon, Need to Upgrade Customers, says CEO Kiran Rathee New Delhi: Bharti Airtel expects its average revenue per user (ARPU) to cross 300, helped by a surge in the share of postpaid customers to 20% over the long term from about 8% now, chief executive officer and managing director Shashwat Sharma said. "I believe it's around the corner... We can go much beyond 300 as well," Sharma told ET in his first interview since taking charge early this year.

Airtel currently has an industry-leading ARPU of 264. The company had 30 million postpaid subscribers as of June 30, accounting for about 8% of its customer base, and added nearly 1.05 million postpaid users during the quarter, its highest quarterly addition. It is betting on initiatives such as Fastlane and tweaking of tariffs to nudge a segment of its about 346.5 million pre-paid subscribers to upgrade to postpaid. "We believe we need to upgrade a lot of customers," Sharma said, describing postpaid upgrades as "a great lever in the industry." Postpaid accounts for about 12% of Airtel's revenue, he noted.

The quarterly pace of postpaid additions has accelerated from roughly 800,000 to about 1-1.1 million in the reported first quarter, an increase of around 30%. When asked about Airtel's recent tariff hike of 50 for postpaid plans, Sharma said, "People have to pay for consumption... Entry-level, inclusive plans have to stay where they are." His comments point to two opportunities for revenue growth: persuading more subscribers to choose richer postpaid packages and restructuring industry tariffs so that customers pay more as their data consumption increases.

Airtel recently launched its Fast Lane service, promising superior network quality based on 5G-slicing technology. The carrier is also seeking to drive upgrades through packages combining data, family connections, entertainment and international roaming benefits. Sharma said family plans offer particular value when households add second and third connections.

The opportunity, he said, lies in offering differentiated experiences that encourage customers to upgrade. Citing Indonesia and the Philippines as examples, Sharma said tiers of plans ranging from small to extra-large and a better pricing structure could allow the industry to sustain annual ARPU growth of 5-7%.

Asked whether Reliance Jio's upcoming public market listing could lead to fewer discounts and a change in telecom pricing, he said, "I think that's a big capital market event in the country. It's an industry problem." Beyond mobile services, Sharma expressed confidence in the data centre business. Asked about the planned expansion to 1 GW of capacity, he said anchor demand and healthy returns could make it a strong long-term business. "The business has very healthy returns," he said, explaining that while capital is invested upfront, returns accrue over a long period. "It pays off for 20-25 years." Himanshi Lohchab contributed to this article

data.title: West Asia Conflict Takes Some Sheen Off Bengal Puja Pandals
data.description:
Writankar Mukherjee Kolkata: The West Asia crisis is casting a shadow over West Bengal's 65,000 crore Durga Puja economy, with major organisers reporting a 10-20% drop in corporate sponsorships this year as companies rein in festive marketing budgets to cope with rising input costs and heightened volatility.

Several large national brands, traditionally among the biggest sponsors of community pujas in Kolkata, have cut spending on below-the-line activities, including sponsorships, promotional kiosks and outdoor advertising, organisers and industry executives said. Kolkata-based brands are stepping up to fill the gap, but their increased spending is insufficient to offset the shortfall in funding from national corporations, puja organisers said.

Parle Products vice president Mayank Shah said the biscuit maker has cut its Puja branding budget by 10-15% this year due to cost pressures. "We want to ensure that selling prices or MRPs are not increased at a time when demand is shaping up well," said Shah. "However, there is a fresh round of input cost pressure, so we have to balance it through internal efficiencies, absorbing a bit and reducing our promotional budget." Angshu Mallick, executive deputy chairman at Fortune edible maker AWL Agri Business said brands are cutting costs as the outlook remains uncertain due to West Asia volatility. The company has been a major sponsor of Bengal's Durga Puja.

LG, Daikin, ITC, Emami, Dabur, PepsiCo, Reliance Consumer Products, Coca-Cola, Xiaomi, Oppo and Vivo ranked among the prominent sponsors of Kolkata pujas.

This year, however, most have cut back on spending on below-the-line activities. Corporate funding is 10-15% lower than last year, said Saswata Basu, vice president of Forum for Durgotsab, an association of community pujas in Kolkata and its suburbs. "A lot of national sponsors are silent," said Basu. "Some want LED signages for outdoor advertising, but only a few pujas have managed to organise it." The Puja festivities officially begin this Saturday and will continue for ten days, with peak celebrations next week.

Kolkata has around 3,000 community pujas, while West Bengal has around 45,000. Local brands are seeking to capitalise on the festival. Lux Industries, Bisk Farm and Spencer's Retail have stepped up promotional efforts, with Bisk Farm increasing its Durga Puja marketing budget by 50% year-on-year.

data.title: Poonawalla Fincorp Q2 Net Up Five-fold
data.description:
SOARS TO 375 CR on strong loan growth Our Bureau Mumbai: Poonawalla Fincorp's second-quarter net profit rose more than five-fold to 375 crore from a year earlier, as rapid loan-book growth lifted interest and fee income and helped operating profit more than double.

The non-bank lender's profit after tax rose 405.2% year-on-year in the quarter ended September 30, from 74 crore a year earlier. Profit increased 21.8% quarter-on-quarter from 308 crore in the preceding quarter. Net interest income, including fees and other income, climbed 75.6% year-on-year to 1,589 crore.

data.title: IT Cos Surge Despite US Immigration Curbs
data.description:
Our Bureau Mumbai: IT stocks surged on Friday, with the Nifty IT index gaining more than 3%, as investors brushed aside fresh uncertainty over the US government's move to bar eight technology companies, including five from India, from participating in a programme linked to employment-based green card applications.

OpenAI's lower-than-estimated revenue run rate and Tata Consultancy Services' (TCS) relatively firm September-quarter results also helped boost sentiment in the sector, which has been grappling with worries about AI-related business disruptions.

The Nifty IT index's Friday performance was its biggest single-day gain since August 28. TCS shares rose 4.2%. HCL Technologies and Infosys gained around 3% each, while Wipro rose about 2.7% and Tech Mahindra advanced around 1.5%. "The rally in Indian IT stocks appears to reflect factors beyond TCS' Q2 results, which offered some reassurance on earnings resilience but no clear demand inflection," said Kunal Bajaj, research analyst at Choice Institutional Equities. "We see the rally as reflecting earnings resilience and easing AI-disruption concerns more than a fundamental recovery." Media reports cited OpenAI telling investors that its annualised revenue run rate in September was nearly $50 billion, lagging the nearly $70 billion figure indicated in earlier reports. "OpenAI's lower-than-previously indicated revenue run rate, largely reflecting differences in calculation and comparability rather than a clear demand slowdown, may also be easing concerns around AI-led disruption to traditional IT services and highlighting opportunities in enterprise AI implementation, integration and modernisation," said Bajaj.

The IT index has slipped nearly 8% from its August highs, retreating from a 17% rally since early July. The extent of the surge in IT stocks on Friday came as a surprise, as market participants were expecting a sell-off in response to the US government's decision to suspend IT firms from availing the Permanent Labour Certification Programme (PERM), which allows skilled foreign workers to gain permanent residency. "One of the major reasons this news did not hold much gravitas when Indian markets opened is because most Indian IT firms in the US, such as Wipro, TCS and Infosys, owing to stricter regulations and higher costs associated with H-1B visas, have hired fewer personnel from outside the US," said Ravi Singh, chief research officer at Master Capital Services. Bajaj said the PERM suspension will have a limited immediate impact as it affects the employment-based green card pipeline, not existing H-1B work authorisation. The IT index is down 24.6% so far in 2026, compared with a 13.8% decline in the Nifty. Analysts, however, are not rushing to conclude that the worst is over for Indian IT stocks.

data.title: Gold Prices Fall Nearly 4% in a Month, Spurs Selective Buying
data.description:
Sutanuka Ghosal Kolkata: Gold prices have fallen nearly 4% in a month to about 1.47 lakh per 10 grams from 1.53 lakh, prompting selective buying ahead of the peak festive and wedding season as consumers look to make the most of the decline while remaining cautious about overall purchase costs. Lightweight designs, studded pieces and old-gold exchanges are gaining traction, according to industry executives. "The recent correction has encouraged some buying interest in India, although consumers remain price conscious," said Darshan Desai, CEO of Aspect Bullion & Refinery.

He said volatility is expected to persist, with the US economic data, Federal Reserve commentary and currency movements influencing prices, even as festive buying provides some support to the domestic bullion market. Jewellery demand remains resilient across price segments. CaratLane managing director Saumen Bhaumik said that consumers are more deliberate with their spending but remain interested in both value-conscious and premium jewellery.

The extended festive and wedding calendar, along with sustained appetite for diamonds and everyday jewellery, is keeping market sentiment positive, according to him. Mangesh Chauhan, managing director, Sky Gold & Diamonds, which manufactures jewellery for leading brands such as Tanishq and Malabar Gold & Diamonds, said festive and wedding demand were expected to remain healthy, supported by strong business-to-business orders from wholesalers and continued store expansion by jewellery retailers. "While prices are elevated, their relative stability in recent months has given consumers greater confidence to plan their purchases," he said.

However, buyers are increasingly seeking affordability without compromising on design. There is a growing preference for lightweight, lower-carat and design-led jewellery, while old-gold exchanges are allowing consumers to acquire new designs within their budgets, said Chauhan. Studded jewellery is also gaining popularity among younger buyers, prompting manufacturers to expand their offerings in this category.

Supriya Kataria, founder of Kumari Fine Jewellery, said that rising prices were making consumers more selective rather than deterring them from purchasing jewellery altogether. Buyers are showing greater interest in lightweight pieces, lower-carat options and versatile designs that balance aesthetics with affordability. Consumers are also comparing gold prices, making charges, promotional offers and exchange values more closely, with brand trust playing an important role in purchase decisions, she said.

The shift is likely to be more pronounced in discretionary purchases, while weddings, festivals and family milestones continue to underpin demand. Old-gold exchanges are emerging as an important means of managing purchase costs, allowing households to use the value of existing jewellery toward new purchases. With the festive and wedding calendar extending over the coming weeks, industry executives expect demand to hold up, though purchase decisions may take longer as consumers balance emotional spending with budget constraints.

data.title: Hurricane Isaias Makes Landfall in Florida — WSJ
data.description:
By Joseph Pisani

Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin, Fla., Friday night, bringing heavy rains, damaging winds and the possibility of life-threatening flooding to the region.

"Buckle down at this point," Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said. "Don't be getting out on the roads."

The Category 2 hurricane hit the U.S. Gulf Coast around 9:30 p.m. Eastern time with 105 mph winds, pulling out trees and knocking down power lines.

More than 500,000 customers in Alabama and Florida were without power Friday night, according to PowerOutage.com, which tracks outages. Utility companies said they would send out crews to make repairs when it was safe to do so.

"Residents in these areas should have a safe room to ride out the storm and prepare for long-duration power outages," the National Weather Service said.

Forecasters warned storm surges could reach as high as 5 feet in parts of Alabama and Florida, moving rising water inland from the coastline. Even normally dry areas near the coast could see dangerous surges.

As much as 8 inches of rainfall is expected this weekend in southern Alabama, the Florida Panhandle and southwest Georgia, increasing the risk of flash flooding, the weather service said.

The hurricane is expected to weaken as it moves inland Saturday, "but Isaias is expected to continue producing gusty winds well inland," the National Weather Service said.

Isaias is the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 in what has been a relatively quiet season.

data.title: Kuwait selects consultant for $7.1mln real estate re-tendering contract
data.description:
Kuwait Authority for Partnership Projects (KAPP) has selected a preferred bidder for a 2.15 million Kuwaiti dinar ($7.1 million) consultancy contract to prepare feasibility studies and oversee the re-tendering of 23 real estate projects on state-owned land, according to local Arabic-language newspaper Al-Qabas.

The preferred bidder was selected from three shortlisted international consulting consortia, the report published on Thursday said.

KAPP has referred the selection to the State Audit Bureau for approval before signing the contract, with a response expected in the coming weeks.

The report did not disclose the identities of the bidders.

The projects list for retendering, according to a previous notice issued in January 2026, include the Fahaheel Waterfront Development (Al Kout); the Waterfront Development Project - Phase Five (Marina Mall); two construction waste treatment plants; Al-Duwalia Centre Project; Al-Mutahida Market; Al-Maseel Market; Al-Kabeer Market; Al-Watiya Market; Kuwait Market; Block 11 (Kuwait Magic); Al-Farwaniya Slaughterhouse; Al-Wataniya Market; Al-Duwali Golf Club; Al-Safat Market; Al-Manakh Market; Al-Duwalia Building Property; Meat and Vegetable Market in Al-Jleeb; Al-Jahra Slaughterhouse; Souq Al-Mubarakiya; Al-Ahmadi Slaughterhouse; Meat and Vegetable Market in Al-Jahra ‘Al-Khaima Mall and Central Fruit and Vegetable Market (Al-Sulaibiya).

The re-tendering initiative aims to increase returns from state-owned properties and expand private-sector participation in their operation, maintenance and development.

data.title: Politically motivated decisions will deeply harm US: Indian-American Congressman Thanedar on Trump's H-1B, Green Card move
data.description:
Michigan, Oct. 10 -- Indian-American Congressman Shri Thanedar has criticised the Trump administration's decision to suspend certain companies from the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) programme, opposing restrictions affecting H-1B visa holders seeking Green Cards and warning that the move could harm the United States' economic innovation.

In a post on X on Friday (local time), Thanedar, a member of the US House Homeland Security Committee, said he strongly disagreed with the administration's decision to suspend the ability of H-1B visa holders working for major technology companies to apply for Green Cards.

"As a proud immigrant and a member of the Homeland Security Committee, I strongly disagree with the Trump Administration's decision to suspend the ability for H-1B visa holders who work for major tech companies to apply for Green Cards," Thanedar said.

He said H-1B workers were highly skilled professionals who made significant contributions to the American economy, adding that the programme played a key role in maintaining the country's global leadership in economic innovation.

"H-1B workers are highly skilled workers who make incredible contributions to America, and this program is a key way our country continues to be the world's leader in economic innovation," he said.

Thanedar called on the Trump administration to use existing laws to address fraud and abuse, increase the Green Card cap and expand funding for training American workers in the technology sector.

"If the President truly wants to combat fraud and increase economic innovation, he should use existing laws to curb fraud and abuse, increase the Green Card cap, and increase funding to train American workers in the tech sector," he said.

He further warned that decisions driven by political considerations could undermine the country's technological competitiveness and its ability to counter China's growing influence.

"Making politically motivated decisions about these important programs that help tech companies maintain America's world-class innovation and to effectively stand up to increasing Chinese aggression will deeply harm America," Thanedar added.

His remarks come amid a broader debate in the United States over the H-1B visa programme and the Trump administration's action against companies applying for permanent labour certifications for foreign workers.

On Thursday (local time), US Labour Secretary Keith Sonderling announced the suspension of certain major technology and IT outsourcing companies from the PERM programme, citing multiple active federal investigations. The companies named included Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL and Capgemini, along with US technology companies Microsoft and Adobe.

Sonderling said the department would neither accept new applications nor process pending permanent labour certification applications involving the companies.

The announcement followed remarks by US Vice President JD Vance, who alleged widespread fraud in the H-1B visa programme and argued that companies should prioritise American workers. Vance specifically cited Microsoft, alleging that the company had laid off American employees while benefiting from thousands of H-1B visas and Green Cards.

Meanwhile, Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) clarified on Friday that the suspension of certain companies from the PERM programme was distinct from the H-1B visa programme and did not, by itself, affect the validity of existing H-1B visas or the status of visa holders and their dependents.

During a weekly media briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the decision could, however, affect the permanent-residency process of eligible employees at the companies concerned.

"The suspension of PERM application does not by itself affect the validity of H-1B visas or the status of H-1B visa holders and their dependents," Jaiswal said, adding that "there could be some impact on the permanent residency or green card process of eligible employees of the affected companies."

Responding to Vance's remarks about the programme, Jaiswal said comments that failed to recognise the contribution of Indian professionals to the American economy were unwarranted.

He also criticised the terminology used to refer to foreign workers, saying, "Resorting to terminology that carries painful historical and colonial legacy connotations is deeply offensive."

The MEA emphasised that the movement of skilled professionals benefits both countries by supporting innovation, research, productivity, competitiveness and job creation.

"Talent mobility adds value to both economies, that is, the economies of India and the United States. While it creates opportunities for Indians, it equally helps US companies with cutting-edge talent, innovation, research, productivity, competitiveness, and job creation," Jaiswal said.

"The steps announced by the US do not advance the shared ambitions of both countries," he added, reiterating India's position that talent mobility remains an area of mutual benefit for New Delhi and Washington.

data.title: India central bank takes steps to support rupee, opens dollar window for oil companies
data.description:
India's central bank has announced more measures to support the rupee on Saturday after the currency fell to within striking distance of its record low.

  • The Reserve Bank of India will open a special window to meet the daily dollar requirements of three government oil-marketing companies to ease the pressure on the spot market

  • Under such an arrangement, used in times of strain on the currency, the RBI provides oil companies dollars directly from its foreign exchange reserves

  • Indian Oil , Hindustan Petroleum and Bharat Petroleum will be allowed to access to access dollars under the facility from Monday, the RBI said

  • Forex dealers will not permit users to rebook any foreign exchange derivatives, the bank said

  • The RBI slashed the limit for positions in exchange-traded currency derivatives involving the rupee to $5 million from $100 million

  • The central bank asked forex dealers to maintain a "foreign exchange risk reserve" for all derivative contracts involving the rupee equal to 20% of the notional amount of each transaction

  • The RBI has raised dollars and hiked its policy rate, but pressure on the currency has persisted. On Friday, the rupee closed at 96.73 per dollar, barely changed from its previous close, and near its all-time weakest level of 96.96, hit in May

  • The rupee rallied in the non-deliverable forward market on Saturday, with the one-month dollar/rupee contract falling about 40 paise in very thin trading, one trader said

  • Addressing oil companies' dollar requirements removes one of the largest sources of demand from the FX market, which should help reduce volatility but it will show up in a depletion of reserves, said Dhiraj Nim, FX strategist at ANZ Bank in Mumbai

data.title: RBI revises forex derivative rules: What changes for transactions, cancelled contracts
data.description:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on October 10 announced regulatory measures for the foreign exchange market, including restrictions on rebooking cancelled foreign exchange derivative contracts, a reduction in transaction thresholds and the introduction of a Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR).

The measures were announced through two circulars, A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 25 and A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 26, with the stated objective of ensuring the orderly functioning of the foreign exchange market.

Restrictions on rebooking cancelled contracts

Authorised dealers will not be permitted to allow users to rebook any foreign exchange derivative contract involving the Indian rupee, whether deliverable or non-deliverable, if it has been cancelled with any authorised dealer after the issuance of the directions.

Rollover of foreign exchange derivative contracts on maturity will continue to be permitted, subject to existing regulatory provisions.

Threshold reduced to $5 million

The RBI has reduced the threshold for undertaking foreign exchange derivative transactions to hedge contracted exposures without establishing the existence of the underlying exposure from $100 million to $5 million equivalent across all authorised dealers.

The corresponding threshold for taking positions in exchange-traded currency derivatives involving the rupee, without establishing the existence of underlying exposure, has also been reduced from $100 million to $5 million equivalent across all recognised stock exchanges taken together.

Additional documentation requirement

Authorised dealers will be required to obtain and retain an undertaking from users entering into rupee-involving foreign exchange derivative contracts to hedge contracted exposures. The undertaking must confirm that the same underlying exposure has not been hedged with any other authorised dealer.

Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve introduced

The RBI has introduced a Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve requirement for rupee-involving foreign exchange derivative contracts with a notional value exceeding $2 million equivalent.

Authorised dealers will be required to maintain a cash reserve with the RBI equal to 20% of the rupee equivalent of the notional amount of each such transaction.

The reserve requirement will apply to rupee-involving foreign exchange derivative contracts undertaken to hedge current account exposures where the user purchases foreign currency against the rupee.

The RBI said the measures are intended to strengthen market discipline, ensure appropriate risk management and maintain an orderly and transparent foreign exchange market.
